doc.name: worldlens: the corner cases no surveyed document happens to contain

$comment: Four rules of the language need a document that decides them, and no surveyed site happens to. A TIE: the station stands at [0, 0] and the two presentation points sit 900 steps away on either side, so only the tie-break can choose, and `a0000000-…` sorts below `b0000000-…`. A CLOSED INTERVAL: the east-half region's edges fall exactly on two cell centres, which a half-open rule would drop. AN EMPTY LIST: one sector names nobody and one names the west point, so `exists` has to say whether an empty list is a statement. THE REFERENCE FORMS: one entity spells out every way the format names another entity — a bare identity, a {generator, key} derivation address, a flat list of both — beside the three spellings that name nothing: a template-local handle, an [x, y] position, and an array inside an array, which is no form of the reader's and is not flattened into one. A DOTTED COMPONENT NAME: the last entity carries both `go.easyloop` and `go`, and each spells out a `station` field at the same dotted path, so `ref(x, y, "go.easyloop.station")` has to say which name it read. Two frames deep on purpose, so `in_frame` has a chain to walk.
